recent_posts.title: Software 2.0: Planning and Verifying a Greenfield Project
recent_posts.summary: A detailed case study on building a greenfield SaaS product (TextForge, an AI email automation tool) using LLM-driven development practices the author calls 'Software 2.0.' Key techniques covered include: using Claude Code's planning mode to define requirements and architecture before writing code, providing reference architectures (DrawTogether.NET) to guide LLM output style, creating reusable agent skill files for non-obvious patterns, writing PRDs for feature scoping, and building a verification pipeline with static analysis, automated tests, snapshot testing via Verify, and Aspire MCP-powered browser automation. The post also discusses incremental refactoring to prevent code quality decay and the tradeoffs of LLM-authored tests. The project passed a CASA2 security audit despite being nearly 100% LLM-written code.

recent_posts.title: Deep inheritance hierarchies create unmaintainable software
recent_posts.summary: Deep inheritance hierarchies create unmaintainable codebases through cognitive overload and "everything touches everything" architectures. The author examines real-world examples including a five-layer inheritance hierarchy for a payment page and an 866-line generic repository, demonstrating how preemptive framework design leads to rigid abstractions that resist change. The solution is to extract patterns after solving problems multiple times, prefer composition over inheritance, and remain skeptical of deep hierarchies beyond two or three layers.

recent_posts.title: Building custom validation grammars with HTML comments and HtmlAgilityPack
recent_posts.summary: A detailed walkthrough of building LinkValidator, a CLI tool for validating HTML links in CI/CD pipelines. The article demonstrates implementing inline HTML comment-based validation control using HtmlAgilityPack, allowing developers to selectively suppress link validation directly in HTML rather than maintaining separate configuration files. Covers the implementation details of parsing HTML comments, handling edge cases, and the design philosophy of keeping validation rules contextual to content.

recent_posts.title: AI coding assistants create unprecedented opportunities for junior developers
recent_posts.summary: AI coding assistants are creating unprecedented opportunities for junior developers to accelerate their learning and productivity while potentially displacing expensive, slow senior developers who resist adaptation. The author argues that AI tools function as mentorship-as-a-service, allowing newcomers to rapidly gain experience shipping real software and learning new technologies. However, this advantage window is temporary due to current VC subsidies that keep AI tools affordable, and junior developers should capitalize on this moment to build real experience and develop technical taste before the opportunity closes.

recent_posts.title: Microsoft deleted third party NuGet packages without notice over security vulnerability
recent_posts.summary: Microsoft deleted NuGet packages from third-party developers without notice to address a security vulnerability in their Microsoft.Identity.Client package. The vulnerability was a typo in XML documentation pointing to a phishing URL, not a critical runtime issue. This action bypassed normal CVE disclosure processes and created concerns about package availability guarantees, Microsoft's privileged access to NuGet operations, and the arbitrary nature of the deletions. The incident highlights tensions between security remediation and package ecosystem stability.

recent_posts.title: Continuous Deployment of Docker Compose Applications Using GitHub Actions
recent_posts.summary: Learn how to continuously deploy Docker Compose applications using GitHub Actions and Tailscale. The post explains the workflow, benefits of Tailscale for secure networking, and provides a comprehensive GitHub Actions file to automate Docker image building and deployment. A detailed breakdown of files and steps ensures you can replicate the setup efficiently.

recent_posts.title: Signing NuGet Packages Using Azure DevOps and Workload Identity Federation
recent_posts.summary: This guide details the process of signing NuGet packages using Azure DevOps and Workload Identity Federation. It addresses the recent challenges caused by updates to Azure VM images and how to transition from using outdated tools like SignClient to the newer dotnet sign, while avoiding the complexities associated with Azure service principals by utilizing managed identities. The guide provides PowerShell scripts and Azure DevOps YAML configurations for setting up and using managed identities and workload identity federation for seamless and secure operations.

recent_posts.title: The Future of AI Belongs to Experienced Operators with Good Taste
recent_posts.summary: The effectiveness of AI in software development is heavily reliant on the experience and skill of the user rather than just the AI itself. While AI can significantly expedite the execution phase, it is not a substitute for in-depth knowledge and expertise. The phenomenon of 'vibe coding' demonstrates that without proper guidance, AI-generated code can result in subpar or even faulty outputs. Experienced operators are essential in steering AI to produce reliable and maintainable solutions.

recent_posts.title: Software Falsehoods: you can build it cheap, fast, and good - pick two
recent_posts.summary: The idea that software development can be cheap, fast, and good is a fallacy. Price is not directly tied to quality or speed. Value in software development is difficult to assess, and success depends more on methodology and organizational fit than on cost. Effective development practices, proper team dynamics, and measuring key performance indicators play a crucial role in delivering high-quality software efficiently.

recent_posts.title: The future of open source sustainability in .NET
recent_posts.summary: FluentAssertions, a popular open source .NET library, changed its license from Apache 2.0 to a commercial model, causing significant community uproar. This post discusses the implications of this change, explores the broader question of whether developers prefer 're-license or die,' and underlines the importance of community engagement for the sustainability of open source projects.
